runs.t: Partitioning splits a dataset into manageable segments; sharding distributes segments across nodes. Both seek scale or manageability but complicate routing and operations.

Choose a partition key based on access patterns, distribution and growth. Consider range, hash and time-based partitioning; plan rebalancing, global uniqueness, cross-shard joins and hotspot prevention.
A multi-tenant platform may partition records by tenant and date. Large tenants can still create hotspots, so test whether tenant-only routing remains balanced as customers grow.
Sharding is usually a late optimization, not an initial design badge. It makes global reporting, transactions and migrations harder; partition pruning depends on queries using partition keys.
